item.title: Sweden’s Andersson Ends Government-Formation Talks Without Result
item.description: Sweden’s election winner Magdalena Andersson said she isn’t able to form a government, underscoring how difficult building a coalition in the fragmented parliament is.
item.dc:creator: Charlie Duxbury

item.title: Japan’s Takaichi Touts Sweeping Changes in Immigration Rules
item.description: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi took to social media over the weekend touting efforts to revise the country’s rules related to foreign nationals, days before some of those rules come into effect.
item.dc:creator: Sakura Murakami

item.title: Trump Rejects Iran's Hormuz Offer as US Borrowing Costs, Oil Rise
item.description:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. Live from Brussels, we set the agenda for your day, catching you up with overnight markets news from the US and Asia. And we'll tell you what matters for investors in Europe, giving you insight before trading begins.
Bonds and stocks dropped after President Donald Trump rejected Iran’s latest proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, denting some of the optimism that lifted markets late last week. Oil rose and precious metals sold off.
The US and China detailed a plan to cut tariffs on about $30 billion of imports from each country, as the superpower rivals take steps to steady ties following a summit between leaders Donald Trump and Xi Jinping.
And Britain’s governing Labour Party gathers in Liverpool for its annual conference ahead of the budget next month.
Today's guests: Martin Heydon, Irish, Agriculture Minister; Rain Newton-Smith, CBI, CEO. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: What Europe’s Data Center Energy Labels Mean for Hyperscalers
item.description: The European Union has dived into the growing debate over data centers with a new sustainability label that will show, among over things, how much power and water a plant is using. Caitilin McManus, a data center analyst at BloombergNEF, joins Daybreak Europe to discuss the move and what it means for hyperscalers and others looking to expand in Europe. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: UK's Burnham and Healey Face High-Stakes Moment
item.description: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham and Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey face a high-stakes moment at the Labour Party's annual conference, as they seek to pivot from the boosterish optimism of Burnham’s early days as premier to a tougher message of tax rises and spending restraint. Bloomberg's Caroline Hepker reports from Liverpool. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: UK's Healey Must Outline Detailed Growth Plan, CBI Says
item.description: Rain Newton-Smith, Confederation of British Industry chief executive officer, discusses what to expect from Chancellor of the Execequer John Healey's speech at the annual Labour Party conference and in his upcoming budget in October. "We need to see that detailed implementation of a growth plan," Newton-Smith says. She speaks with Bloomberg's Caroline Hepker from Liverpool, where the Labour Party is hosting its annual conference. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: London’s Waterloo Bridge at Risk of Shutdown Within Three Years
item.description: Britain’s river crossings face growing strain from heavy traffic, extreme weather and funding shortages. Now some of London’s bridges really are falling down.
item.dc:creator: Harry Black

item.title: Here’s the List of Goods the US, China Agreed on for Tariff Cuts
item.description: The US and China released lists of the $30 billion worth of goods they plan to cut tariffs on, though without providing details on how much levies would be slashed.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: US Midterms Won't Shift China Tensions: Eurasia's Wang
item.description: Eurasia Group China Director Dan Wang argues that upcoming US midterm elections will not alter relations with Beijing, as executive policy and tech export controls remain the primary drivers. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US, China Release Product Lists for $30 Billion Tariff Deal
item.description: The US and China detailed a plan to cut tariffs on about $30 billion of imports from each country, as the superpower rivals take steps to steady ties following a summit between leaders Donald Trump and Xi Jinping.
item.dc:creator: Nectar Gan

item.title: Seoul Demands Ukraine Apology Over North Korea POW Disclosure
item.description: Seoul demanded an official apology and explanation from Kyiv, accusing Ukraine of violating an agreement to keep confidential the transfer of North Korean prisoners of war to South Korea.
item.dc:creator: Heesu Lee

item.title: Jollibee’s Global IPO Can Wait
item.description: Jollibee plans to spin off its fast-growing international business and list it in Hong Kong. Bloomberg Opinion columnist Juliana Liu says the split makes sense, but the overseas operation needs at least another year to prove it can stand on its own. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: French Conservatives to Keep Senate Majority as Far Right Gains
item.description: France’s conservative Republicans party and its allies were set to retain a majority in the Senate, even as the populist National Rally gained several seats and boosted its position in the upper house.
item.dc:creator: Alan Katz and Samy Adghirni

item.title: Labour’s Alexander Says Burnham Can Tackle UK Challenges
item.description: UK Secretary of State for Scotland Douglas Alexander spoke to Bloomberg Television at the annual Labour Party Conference in Liverpool, saying that "there's a recognition that we face big constraints and big structural challenges" but that he personally welcomes Burnham's plans around social care. He also commented on the UK's relationship with the US in light of the RAF Fairford incident in the UK, saying he assures that the intelligence sharing relationships between the US, US, and allies across the West "is as strong as it's ever been." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Policy on Taiwan Is Unchanged After Xi’s Visit, Perdue Says
item.description: Donald Trump and Xi Jinping discuss Taiwan arms sales every time they get together but the American stance on the self-ruled island remains unchanged following the Chinese leader’s state visit to Washington last week, the US president’s top envoy to Beijing said.
item.dc:creator: Phila Siu

item.title: Swiss Reject Stricter Neutrality, Preserving Government Leeway
item.description: Swiss voters rejected a bid to enshrine stricter neutrality in the constitution, preserving the government’s freedom to interpret the doctrine flexibly and maintain sanctions against Russia.
item.dc:creator: Bastian Benrath-Wright

item.title: Russia Hits Ukraine Data Centers in Barrage That Killed Six
item.description: Russian airstrikes overnight and early Sunday killed at least six people across Ukraine and targeted a number of major data centers in Kyiv, officials said.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: UK Terrorism Police Investigate Incident Near US Air Base, Arrest Five Men
item.description: UK police were investigating a potential terrorism incident after five men were arrested near an air base used in US strikes on Iran, with President Donald Trump saying the suspects were “looking to do big damage” to the facility.
item.dc:creator: Alex Wickham and Angela Cullen

item.title: Iran Says Won’t Soften Demands After Trump Rejects Hormuz Offer
item.description: Iran stuck to its seven-day proposal for reopening the crucial Strait of Hormuz, saying it won’t soften its conditions, while President Donald Trump sent mixed signals about his willingness to reach a deal.
item.dc:creator: Eltaf Najafizada and Courtney Subramanian

item.title: Serb President Vucic to Quit in Switch to PM Post, Echoing Putin’s Power Move
item.description: Embattled Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic resigned on Sunday in a well-telegraphed move as he seeks to transition to the role of prime minister as a way of staying close to power in the Balkan nation.
item.dc:creator: Jasmina Kuzmanovic and Jan Bratanic
